summary: Rudolf Much was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1883 to 1887 and held a post there from circa 1892 to 1936.

Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1888–1889) and under Richard von Garbe, later holding posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and University of Marburg (~1917–1929).

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1877–1878) and under Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübinger Stift (~1839–1843) under Heinrich Ewald and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843–1844), later serving at the University of Tübingen as Privatdozent (1845) and Extraordinarius (1848–1895).

Rudrapatna Shamasastry worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Madras, Calcutta, Oriental University, and Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, he served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College (1912–1918), Curator at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929), and Mysore Archaeological Director (1926).

Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University (PhD attested 2018) under supervisors including Paul Harrison and Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and holds a post at the University of Heidelberg.

Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), subsequently serving on the faculty at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins, served as President of the Pali Text Society (2003), and held posts at the University of Bristol beginning in 1987.

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Nagoya University. She has held research posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1998, 2015) and the Eastern Institute (attested 2015).

Ruth Fuller Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at the University of Chicago and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki and Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, later serving as director of the Buddhist Society of America and abbess of Ryōsen-an.

Ruth Gamble is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at the Australian National University (by 2014) supervised by John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman. She held posts at ANU and the University of Munich.

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi (1987–1988), and was appointed James P. Storer Associate Professor at Kenyon College.

Ryan Anningson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and completed his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Naropa University, earning a Master of Arts in Religious Studies under teachers including Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, and Sarah Harding.

Ryan Richard Overbey works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Educated at Brown and Harvard (PhD 2010), he has held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, UC Berkeley (2013–2015), Holy Cross, and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).
Ryodo Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a researcher post at Taisho University (attested 2015–2020) and a part-time lecturer post at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Berlin. He lectured at the University of Berlin and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1974).
Ryoichi Kondo was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryojin Soga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University (1916–1924) and as a professor and 17th president (1961–1967) of Otani University.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
